title: region-tethering-ops-notes-and-risk-log
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notes + risk log for the ‘region tethering’ approach (soft-first enforcement) for customer region pin requests. Goal is to capture operational steps, detection signals, fallback paths, and legal/contract escalations in one lightweight doc for SRE, Oncall, and Sales Eng to reference during pilot rollouts.

Background / why this exists:
- We have many overlapping residency playbooks (hard pin, soft pin, anchor) floating across docs. This file experiments with calling the model-location constraint ‘tethering’ to distinguish from existing 'pin' docs and to focus on operator-first enforcement patterns.
- Intended for early pilot customers who need stronger evidence that traffic remained within a region, but want minimal disruption during enforcement ramp.

Scope & constraints:
- Applies only to Redwood Private deployments and Dedicated clusters with regional affinity enabled.
- Not intended to change the API surface for customers; enforcement is implemented in routing and operator tooling.
- Must support: audit evidence generation, automatic sampling for exceptions, and operator-assisted hardening.
- Compliance goal: produce tamper-evident routing logs + KV evidence for audit windows (30/90/365d depending on contract).

Definitions (for this doc):
- Tethered request: an incoming request with a tenant region claim and routing decision that prefers local region only; may fall back if local capacity lacks model or GPU type.
- Soft-tether: policy that prefers local region but allows fallback to alternate region under controlled conditions and records evidence.
- Hard-tether: strict enforcement that rejects/fails requests when local region unavailable.

High-level enforcement model proposal (soft-first):
1) Evaluate tenant region claim at ingress. Add region tag to request metadata.
2) If local region has compatible model variant within version tolerance -> route local.
3) If model variant missing or capacity saturated, allow fallback to pre-approved alt-region per customer contract with evidence collection.
4) Mark request with decision code (LOCAL_ALLOWED | FALLBACK_APPROVED | FALLBACK_BLOCKED) and append signed routing proof (HMAC over route metadata using cluster key).
5) Operators review periodic artifacts for policy drift; escalation to legal when fallback ratio > threshold.

API / telemetry contract changes (ops-visible only):
- New response headers for internal use: X-RW-Region-Decision, X-RW-Route-Proof (base64).
- Internal event schema additions: region_claim, route_decision, fallback_reason (if any), hmac_proof, model_variant_id, gpu_class.
- Sampling mode toggles per-customer via feature flag (ff_region_tethering_sample_pct).

Operator runbook (day-to-day):
- Alerting triggers:
  * tether-fallback-rate > 1% sustained over 30m (pager to SRE)
  * route-proof-signing-failure count > 5 in 10m (pager)
  * telemetry dropouts for region_claim field > 0.5% (page)
- Immediate triage steps: check cluster capacity dashboard -> model catalog mapping -> KMS health (signing keys) -> recent config changes (PRs).
- If fallbacks > threshold for a customer: open scoped incident, notify Sales Eng & CSM, enable stricter sampling and collect 1h of full request traces for legal review.
- Reverting to soft-mode: set ff_region_tethering_sample_pct to 100% (collect) and ff_region_tethering_enforce=false. Hard rejections only via documented change with approval from PM + Legal.

Evidence packaging for audits:
- For each tethered request sample, generate simple JSON blob: ts, tenant_id, client_ip (obfuscated), region_claim, final_route_region, model_variant, decision_code, proof_sig. Store blobs in time-partitioned S3 (region-specific buckets) and run integrity job to produce SHA256 manifest for auditors.
- Retention tiers (per-contract): 30d (standard), 90d (enterprise), 365d (regulated).

Risk matrix (short):
- Incorrect region_claim mapping -> customer complaint / breach risk. Mitigation: add a tenant-region-sanity-check step in onboarding and allow customers to assert via API endpoint (tenant.region.assert).
- Signing key compromise -> evidence forgery. Mitigation: rotate signing keys quarterly, HSM/KMS usage, and distinct signing scopes per-region.
- Telemetry gaps -> inability to prove compliance. Mitigation: sampling fallback to synchronous evidence mode, and operator pager.
- Latency regressions from extra routing checks -> SLO impact. Mitigation: cache region_affinity decisions for 15s per tenant; asynchronous proof signing pipeline.

Migration & rollforward plan for pilot customers (4-week):
Week 0: baseline measurement + enable sampling at 1% (no behavioral change).
Week 1: increase sampling to 10%, begin operator review of samples, fix mapping issues.
Week 2: enable soft-tether routing (allow fallback with proof) at 50% of requests; Sales Eng to notify customers.
Week 3: evaluate fallback ratios and customer feedback. If fallback < 0.5% and evidence patterns stable, schedule hardening window.
Week 4: optional hard-tether trial for specific tenants with legal ok.

Legal questions & open contract items (to confirm with Legal):
- Can we include proof_sig as sufficient evidence in customer SLAs? (Confluence: see linked artifact REGION-TETHERING-PROPOSAL-8812)
- Definitions for acceptable fallback circumstances in T&Cs (capacity, emergency maintenance, model-version mismatch).
- Data export requirements for region-specific evidence buckets (cross-region replication policies).

Experiment ideas / things to A/B test:
- HMAC vs asymmetric signing for evidence proofs (tradeoff: performance vs verifiability).
- TTL for cached region_affinity decisions (5s vs 15s vs 60s) and impact on latency & fallback rate.
- UX for customers to query their evidence (self-serve portal vs on-demand support bundle).

Open action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Evan: add tenant.region.assert API stub (Jira RESID-412) -> PR in ops-config (see linked PR).
- [ ] Priya: draft contract clause for 'approved fallback' scenarios and hand to Legal by 2026-02-25.
- [ ] Liam: capacity mapping job to list which clusters lack which quantized model variants (run daily).
- [ ] Maya (me): build minimal evidence pack generator script for audits, store under ops-scripts/evidence-pack.

Notes to self / informal:
- Want to avoid duplicating existing 'pin' naming to reduce doc confusion — tethering felt distinct and operator-focused.
- Consider including small visualization in Confluence showing request -> route -> proof flow; short GIF would help Sales Eng.
- If we add self-serve evidence portal, need strong rate limits and expensive export paths; careful with costs.

Appendix: example evidence blob (sampled)
{
  "ts": "2026-02-11T14:23:05Z",
  "tenant_id": "acct_7fG3",
  "region_claim": "eu-west-1",
  "route_decision": "FALLBACK_APPROVED",
  "final_route_region": "eu-north-1",
  "model_variant_id": "rw-7b-pt-q4f",
  "decision_reason": "local-capacity-saturated",
  "proof_sig": "MEUCIQDf...base64sig..."
}

Relevant links (quick):
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/REGION-TETHERING-PROPOSAL-8812
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RESID-412 (tenant.assert API work)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/298 (evidence pack sketch)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02TETHER/p1654327890

Last thoughts: keep this doc lightweight; it should live alongside operator runbooks but be explicit about what is experimental. Expect to iterate names/contract language after Legal and Sales Eng feedback.

End of notes.
